(section) Sec. 1, 21-2-218(b.2)(1) (information a registrar sends to the Secretary of State for a registrant who says they were registered in another state)
(quote) (b.2)(1) If a person's voter registration application indicates, pursuant to subsections (a) and (b.1) of this Code section, that such person had previously been registered to vote in a different state, the registrar shall cause the following information of the applicant, if available, to be transmitted to the Secretary of State: (A) Full name; (B) Year of birth; (C) Last four digits of his or her Social Security Number; (D) Driver's license or identification card number; (E) Any unique voter identification number assigned to such applicant; (F) Address of current residence; (G) Address of previous residence; and (H) A copy of the applicant's voter registration form.
(other) Sec. 1: revises 21-2-218 so registrants who moved from another state, county or municipality give information to cancel the old registration, and a signed statement requesting cancellation
(other) Sec. 2: new 21-2-225(e): Secretary of State notifies the other state, with quarterly public report
(other) Sec. 3: revises 21-2-232 (removal of elector name from list; text not summarized further)
(other) effective date added in the substitute
(note) Off this topic: the bill sets no ID or citizenship-proof rule.
